Dashiv Oldest Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Sources disagree on this cemetery's fate: the Commission on the Preservation of Jewish Heritage dates its establishment to the 18th century and its demolition to precisely 1933, yet a local resident recalled two tombstones still standing there as late as the 1950s — a discrepancy worth flagging rather than resolving. Dashiv's Jewish community suffered a sharp decline from 406 people in 1765 to just 270 by 1776, before rebuilding to 1,837 by 1847; the poet and prose writer Israel Wacher, born here in 1892, shares a surname with the town's rabbi from 1885, Aryeh Yehuda-Leib Wacher, though no family connection is confirmed. The community endured two severe pogroms in 1917 and 1919, and 814 Jews from Dashiv and its surrounding areas were executed following the German occupation of July 1941.
